items.title: EU vies to expand role in Ukraine-Russia peace talks to influence US thinking
items.why: Shows how Brussels is trying to stop a US–Russia deal being made over its head, with the Abu Dhabi timing and Moscow's conditions.

items.title: Von der Leyen: a magyar változásokkal Európa is erősebb lett
items.why: Shows how the EU is rewarding [[p:Péter Magyar]]'s reforms with funds, in the same week Budapest held back Ukraine's next clusters.

items.title: With Kyiv's air defense crews as they race to keep up with Russia's jet-powered drones
items.why: Ground-level reporting on why fast jet Shaheds beat Kyiv's layered air defence, and what interceptors are coming.

items.title: Can the US still deter Russia? Lithuania navigates an uneasy alliance
items.why: On-record views from Vilnius on hedging against Washington while seeking permanent US troops; analysis.

items.title: New electronics reach Iran, but prices soar as gov't fees, US sanctions hit
items.why: A reporter in Tehran shows how the blockade and the UAE trade halt reach shop counters: smuggling through Sulaimaniyah, import duties of up to 30%, and a minimum wage of about $83 a month with the rial near 2.64 million per dollar.

items.title: הפעם אנחנו יודעים (This time we know)
items.why: Israel's senior columnist, writing on election eve, sets out what each outcome would mean for war, the judiciary and Arab citizens. He reveals that army chiefs Halevi and Zamir demanded Netanyahu's orders in writing, and argues the opposition should merge after the vote. This is opinion.

items.title: Itamaraty convoca representante da Argentina para explicar passagem de Flávio Bolsonaro pelo país
items.why: Follows the defeated candidate's exit minute by minute from Argentine migration records (bridge crossing, private jet, a flight plan to Guayaquil that ended in Miami), and explains why the summons is a pointed signal while the two countries have had no ambassadors since August.

items.title: Delcy Rodríguez volvió a prometer elecciones en Venezuela, pero no puso fecha y pidió "apoyar las reformas"
items.why: Sets out the interim government's sequence (amnesty, justice reform with EU help, a softer hate-speech law, talks with the 2015 National Assembly) that Caracas says must come before any vote, which matters now that Washington is talking about a 2027 timetable.

items.title: 'The alternative to diplomacy is war': Polisario warns of risks after collapse of Western Sahara UN mission
items.why: The Polisario's own reading of the MINURSO collapse, with Crisis Group on the risk of Algeria being drawn in.

items.title: Deadly RSF drone attacks reveal deep divisions between Sudan and Ethiopia
items.why: Lays out Khartoum's drone data and Addis Ababa's counter-charges behind the consulate expulsions. Most figures are Sudanese government claims.

items.title: The real reason IGP Dan Bahadur Karki was sacked
items.why: Insider-sourced account of how a police-chief dismissal and newsroom raids opened the first public rift in Balen Shah's government. Reasons come from unnamed officials.

items.title: 2026 enlargement report: what it says about Georgia
items.why: Clear chapter-by-chapter walk through the Commission's verdict on Georgia, including its four priority judicial reforms.

items.title: EU rejects Trump's 'big beautiful' security deal with Russia and 'all of Europe'
items.why: Gathers the on-record EU, Polish and Ukrainian replies to Washington's hint of a Europe-wide deal with Moscow, days before Abu Dhabi.

items.title: Budget 2027 rejeté : quelles sont les prochaines étapes au Parlement ?
items.why: The parliament channel's clear map of France's options after both budget bills fell: Senate, joint committee, 49.3, ordinances or a stopgap law.

items.title: Operation Carthage: NABU and SAPO probe SBU corruption
items.why: The fullest account of the fortnight's biggest graft case, alleged protection of scam call centres and drug sales by [[p:Security Service of Ukraine|SBU]] and police officers, with denials and caveats laid out.

items.title: Abu Dhabi talks: why Russia appointed Medinsky and what to expect
items.why: A sober pre-talks read on both delegations and the agenda, using the 2025 Istanbul talks as precedent for why a breakthrough is unlikely. Analysis.

items.title: 'They killed us': Novaya Gazeta announces its closure after decades of repression
items.why: How the state squeezed out Russia's last major independent paper, step by step.

items.title: Ahead of the Knesset swearing-in: agreements, disputes and what the Haredim will do
items.reporter: Moran Azulai, Yuval Karni et al.
items.why: The clearest map of Israel's coalition arithmetic: what Lieberman demands, what UTJ wants on the draft law, and why Shas is the swing problem for [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]].

items.title: Yemen government forces claim new advances as Houthi border attacks resume
items.why: A front-by-front picture of the Saudi–[[p:Houthis|Houthi]] war that separates each side's claims from what can be verified.

items.title: 日中領袖會談喬不攏 共同社：高市恐在APEC受冷落
items.why: Short, clear account of why Beijing is freezing out [[p:Sanae Takaichi]] at APEC and how Xi is expected to rank the US and Russian leaders above Japan in Shenzhen.

items.title: The Dutertes on trial in November: Sara at the Senate, Rodrigo at the ICC
items.why: A Davao-based veteran lays out both trials side by side: which impeachment article survived, the ICC schedule, and what each means for the Duterte camp before 2028.

items.title: Trump and Venezuela's Elusive Elections
items.why: Analysis of how Washington, not Caracas, is steering Venezuela's transition, and why the oil deal leaves [[p:María Corina Machado]] in a bind.

items.title: El Salvador's Presence and a Gang's Offer Test Haiti's Security
items.why: Context on the Salvadoran deployment and the [[p:400 Mawozo]] offer to talk, before this week's strike on its base.

items.title: Taliban–Pakistan border clashes continue, TTP attack kills 10 Pakistani police
items.why: A dated log of the latest border clashes, drawing on Afghan and Pakistani local media. FDD is a hawkish think tank, so read it for the chronology.

items.title: CSTO Without Armenia: What Keeps Yerevan From Leaving and What the Summit Means for Central Asia
items.why: Analysis of why Armenia stays formally inside the [[p:Collective Security Treaty Organization|CSTO]] while boycotting it, and what the Moscow summit means for Central Asian members.

items.title: Babiš a Fico se ohradili vůči výzvě Merze k další finanční podpoře Ukrajiny
items.why: Shows how Prague and Bratislava see Berlin's bid to tie Ukraine funding to the EU budget, in their own words.

items.title: COP31 Bulletin Day 6: Climate marchers call for justice as talks make limited progress
items.why: A clear map of the open fights at [[e:2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference|COP31]] before ministers take over.

items.title: Бій триватиме, але чи і в 2027-му?
items.why: A sober Ukrainian-language look at the fight for Kostiantynivka and Druzhkivka, separating map evidence from a veteran analyst's view, as Putin pitches a 'humanitarian' truce there.

items.title: Zelensky says senior officials named in drug ring tapes have no links to criminal network
items.why: Explains the Khimprom tapes, who is and is not implicated, and why the case reaches into Poland.

items.title: 'No war, no peace': Can Iran break the deadlock with the US?
items.why: Clearest map of where US–Iran diplomacy stands: Tehran's seven conditions, [[p:Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf]]'s 'ball in the US court', Washington's pressure strategy and the risk of miscalculation (analysis).

items.title: Jericho's Palestinian residents fear a settler takeover
items.why: First-hand reporting on how settlers are buying into Palestinian-run towns, a structural West Bank shift that daily violence counts miss (reporter's notebook).

items.title: Gibran's exit leaves Prabowo with expanding power — and Indonesia with questions
items.why: Explains why the vice president's resignation and the police-chief wiretap case matter together: the dismantling of [[p:Joko Widodo]]'s network and how far [[p:Prabowo Subianto]] may centralise power (analysis).

items.title: What is Trump hoping to achieve at APEC meeting in China?
items.why: Primer for the 19 Nov Trump–Xi summit and first US–China–Russia meeting: the trade truce's lagging purchases, the held-up Taiwan arms package and allies' fear of a 'G2' (analysis).

items.title: Carney and Sheinbaum meet at summit in China, as both navigate Trump's tumult
items.why: Clear account of where the [[e:USMCA|United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement]] stands after Washington declined to renew it, and why Ottawa and Mexico City are hedging toward Beijing.

items.title: How SAF successes in Sudan's Kordofan could turn tide against the RSF
items.why: Reported from Khartoum with Sudanese analysts: explains how the West Kordofan push and RSF defections could open the road to Darfur for the [[p:Sudanese Armed Forces]].

items.title: What Happens Next With Western Sahara? No One Knows
items.why: Clearest account of how the [[p:United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara|MINURSO]] wind-down works, with Polisario, UN and analyst views on the risk of war.

items.title: Clock ticking on Ganga Water Treaty, Indian delegation heads to Dhaka but renewal not on agenda
items.why: Sourced explainer on the 12 Dec deadline: Dhaka's demand for a guaranteed dry-season flow, pressure in Bihar to scrap the treaty, and why renewal has stalled.

items.title: NGOs in Azerbaijan face re-registration as experts warn of tighter rules
items.why: Clause-by-clause breakdown of the NGO bill, with Azerbaijani lawyers explaining how suspension and dissolution move from courts to the executive.

items.title: Le Sénat adopte le budget 2027 de la Sécurité sociale en première lecture
items.why: Measure-by-measure guide to what the Senate changed and the 49.3 and ordinance scenarios before the 26 Nov deadline.

items.title: Serbia Still Has a Steep Hill to Climb
items.why: Analysis of whether the [[p:Student List]] can govern, and where it stands on Russia, Kosovo and China.

items.title: Russian Warship Explosion in Libya Destroys Corvette Merkury
items.why: Specialist first account, with satellite imagery, of Ukraine's naval campaign reaching the Mediterranean, and careful about what is still unknown.

items.title: Analyysi: Ukrainan isku venäläislaivaan vaikuttaa Suomenlahdella ainakin neljällä tavalla
items.why: How the Sparta II and Naro-Fominsk strikes bring the war into the Gulf of Finland: shipping, drifting wrecks, oil-spill risk and Estonian alerts.

items.title: What next for Iraq's push against militias following Jurf al-Sakhar deal?
items.why: Explains how Baghdad got [[p:Kata'ib Hezbollah]] to let the state into its stronghold, the reported Iranian role, and why analysts disagree on whether the deal changes anything.

items.title: Yemen's war fronts expand as Houthis attempt to encircle Aden
items.why: Aden-based reporting on the new Al-Bayda–Abyan front, showing how the [[p:Houthis]] could squeeze Aden from two directions rather than storm it.

items.title: 陳吉寧落馬 分析：影響21大人事布局 習近平不打算設接班人
items.why: Three Taiwanese China specialists explain what [[p:Chen Jining]]'s fall means for the 2027 Party Congress line-up and for the Tsinghua network, and why some read it as Xi not planning a successor. Goes further than the English wires.

items.title: Supreme Court partly overturns Han Duck-soo's martial law conviction
items.why: Lays out the court's reasoning on why the [[e:2024 South Korean martial law]] was an insurrection but planning alone did not prove intent, and the dissents. It sets the frame for Yoon Suk Yeol's appeal verdict in January.
